summary: Mario Poceski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2000 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He visited at the University of Iowa in 2001 and joined the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

Mario Praz studied at the universities of Bologna (around 1914–1918) and Florence (around 1918–1920). He held posts at the University of Manchester (around 1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (around 1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Matics studied under Robert A. Fowkes and completed doctoral research supervised by Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler.

Marion Meyer is an archaeologist and historian. Meyer held appointments at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), the University of Florida (1996), the University of Bonn (around 1997–2003), and the University of Vienna (around 2003).

Mark A. Nathan, a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, earned a PhD from UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. In 2010, he held positions at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo.

Mark Allon is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman (around 1990–1994). He served as a research assistant at SOAS (around 1996–2002) before joining the University of Sydney around 2002.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi works in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He was an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (around 1994–2005) before becoming Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at the University of California, Berkeley around 2005.

Mark D. Griffiths earned a BSc from the University of Bradford (around 1984–1987) and a PhD from the University of Exeter (1987–1990). He lectured at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) before becoming Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott is a scholar of sinology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a professor of history at UC Santa Barbara (around 1993–2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University around 2003.

Mark I. Wallace is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul Ricœur (around 1982–1986). After posts at Georgia State University and Merrimack College, he joined Swarthmore College around 1989.

Mark Jan Dresden was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Amsterdam and Utrecht, where his teachers included Jan Gonda. He served on the faculty of the University of Pennsylvania from 1949 to 1977.

Mark Juergensmeyer, a religious studies and Indology scholar, earned a PhD in political science from UC Berkeley (around 1969–1974). He held professorships at the University of California, Santa Barbara (around 1993) and Claremont McKenna College.

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held academic posts within the State University of New York system, including an associate professorship at the University at Albany, SUNY, attested in 2005–2006.
Mark Owen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Leeds under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski was an Indologist and philosopher who earned degrees at Banaras Hindu University, a PhD at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson (around 1974–1979), and a DLitt from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1985.

Mark Siderits is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served on the faculty of Illinois State University from around 1979 to 2008 and later at Seoul National University from around 2008 to 2012.
Mark Singleton is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge and served as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

Mark T. Unno is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College and Stanford University, and has held posts at Brown University and the University of Oregon (around 1998).

Mark Tatz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia in 1978 under Leon Hurvitz. He was a professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 1988).

Mark Teeuwen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who completed his MA and PhD at Leiden University. He lectured at Cardiff University (1994–1999) before becoming a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.
